diagnosis: Schematic representation of the three defined mantle cell neoplasms
legend: In situ mantle cell neoplasm is confined to the mantle zone of the lymph node; the neoplastic cells carry the characteristic t(11;14)(q13;q32) translocation and overexpress both cyclin D1 and SOX11. The variable regions of their IG genes (IGHV) are not mutated. Mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) is characterized by lymph node effacement and the same t(11;14)(q13;q32) translocation as in situ mantle cell neoplasm in most cases, but also complex mutations and copy number variations as indicated. MCL can progress to one of its variants: blastoid or pleomorphic MCL. Leukaemic non-nodal MCL is thought to arise from an IGHV-mutated SOX11-negative cell with characteristic alterations in TP53 and TERT.
